text:
GRAPH NODE (from the document-decomposition graph; translate the node's claim, grounded in its source text)

ESTABLISHES (the one claim this module must express):
When interacting with third parties on behalf of the user (e.g., tool calls, artifacts), the assistant should not lie by commission unless explicitly instructed to do so by the user. However, lies of omission on behalf of the user may be acceptable if they align to general social norms and expectations. The assistant is expected to be honest and forthright, clarifying uncertainty whenever needed and avoiding deceptive behavior.

PROVIDES (use EXACTLY these names as the predicates this module defines):
  (none)

NEEDS -- these concepts are established by OTHER nodes of the graph, so every one of them belongs in this module's `requires`, spelled EXACTLY as given; never in `ontology`, never defined here. `inputs` is only for plain facts about the situation being judged (messages, roles, case data) that YOU identify -- a name can never appear in both requires and inputs:
  (none)

CITATION: every ontology/asserts entry that cites a source must cite EXACTLY 'l2474_2554_n004' -- the id of this node. Never cite line numbers, line ranges, or any other id.

SOURCE TEXT (verbatim from the document; the L-numbers locate text, they are not citable ids):
L2486-L2486:
When interacting with third parties on behalf of the user (e.g., tool calls, artifacts), the assistant should not "lie by commission" unless explicitly instructed to do so by the user. However, lies of omission on behalf of the user may be acceptable if they align to general social norms and expectations. The assistant is expected to be honest and forthright, clarifying uncertainty whenever needed (see [?](#express_uncertainty)) and avoiding deceptive behavior.

CROSS-REFERENCED CLAUSES — the text of every clause this one points at.
Use these to know what the names mean. Do NOT translate them here.

22. Add `clarification_needed/1` to `inputs`.
23. Change the `lie_by_commission` closure to `unclear`, reason "the clause prohibits lying by commission only when the assistant interacts with third parties on the user's behalf, and withdraws even that when the user explicitly instructs it, so its silence is unsettled".
24. Change the `lie_by_omission` closure to `unclear`, reason "the clause permits only omissions that align with general social norms and expectations and leaves other omissions unsettled".

26. Change the `lie_by_commission` read_back to "lying by commission in % should not happen unless the user explicitly instructed it".
27. In claim C1, replace "must not" with "should not".
28. Replace claim C3 with three claims: "the assistant is expected to be honest and forthright", "the assistant is expected to clarify uncertainty whenever needed", and "the assistant is expected to avoid deceptive behavior".
29. Add a claim "the clause states the permission for lies of omission as an exception to its expectation of honesty, and this module does not encode the relation between the two".
